================================================================================
TITLE: Account webhook URL enables full SSRF
FILE: src/accounts.js
LINE: 69
CATEGORY: authorization
SEVERITY: critical
VERDICT: CONFIRMED
PREEXISTING: False
FOUNDBY: ['security']
VERIFIEDBY: ['refute:p1.1', 'refute:p1.2', 'refute:p1.3']
PANEL: 3 of 3 skeptics could not refute it
SUMMARY: setWebhook only checks that the owner-supplied URL parses and has an http/https scheme, so the server later fetches that exact attacker-chosen URL on every deposit, transfer, and close touching the account, letting any plain member proxy requests at arbitrary internal or third-party hosts.
SITES: [{"file": "src/accounts.js", "line": 69, "title": "Account webhook URL enables full SSRF"}]
FAILURE: An authenticated non-admin user (role 'member') opens an account, calls POST /accounts/:id/webhook with { url: 'http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/' } (accepted, 200), then closes that same account (owner-only, no other role needed). I ran this exact sequence against the live server (test harness, fixture user tok-bob) and confirmed the server actually issues an HTTP POST, HMAC-signed with the operator's own webhook secret, to that address: console output was `requests issued, solely by a member acting alone: [ 'https://operator.example/hook', 'http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/' ]`. I separately confirmed via `new URL()` that 127.0.0.1, ::1, 10.0.0.5, localhost, decimal-encoded 2130706433, and hex-encoded 0x7f.0.0.1 all pass the validation in setWebhook unchanged -- none of loopback, link-local, private ranges, or IP-encoding tricks are blocked, and credentials-in-URL (user:pass@host) also pass through untouched. docs/security.md:12-14 states as a standing, self-enforced invariant that 'The service sends HTTP requests to one place only: the webhook endpoint the operator configures. It never requests a URL that a user supplied, in whole or in part,' and docs/security.md:3-4 requires a breaking change to update that file in the same PR; this diff does not touch docs/security.md. Additionally, the delivery fetch (src/webhooks.js's deliver, using global fetch) follows redirects by default, so even a hostname allow-list would need separate handling for redirect-based SSRF, which also is not present.
ROOTCAUSE: setWebhook (src/accounts.js) validates only that the owner-supplied URL parses and has an http/https scheme, with no block on internal/private/link-local hosts, so the notifier (which fetches that exact URL on every deposit, transfer, and close) can be pointed by any member at arbitrary internal or third-party targets — a direct SSRF, and a violation of docs/security.md's explicit invariant that the service never requests a user-supplied URL, confirmed by reproduction (owner's webhookUrl is delivered to verbatim with no host-level checks anywhere in the codebase).
================================================================================
TITLE: Owner webhook equal to operator's causes duplicate delivery
FILE: src/webhooks.js
LINE: 38
CATEGORY: correctness
SEVERITY: medium
VERDICT: CONFIRMED
PREEXISTING: False
FOUNDBY: ['boundary-contract', 'correctness']
VERIFIEDBY: ['refute:1']
PANEL: None
SUMMARY: notify() builds its delivery list as `[url, ...also].filter(Boolean)` with no de-duplication against the operator's own configured `url`, so when an account's owner-set webhookUrl equals the operator's LEDGER_WEBHOOK_URL, the same event is POSTed to that one endpoint twice.
SITES: [{"file": "src/webhooks.js", "line": 38, "title": "Owner webhook equal to operator's causes duplicate delivery"}, {"file": "src/webhooks.js", "line": 37, "title": "Same event double-delivered to a shared webhook URL"}]
FAILURE: Confirmed by direct test against createNotifier: with `url: 'https://hooks.example/ledger'` and `notify('deposit.created', data, ['https://hooks.example/ledger'])`, two separate HTTP POSTs are sent to the identical target, each independently timestamped (`at` differs per call) and independently HMAC-signed, so the receiver cannot tell they are the same underlying deposit — there is no event id/nonce anywhere in the payload (`{ event, data, at }` in src/webhooks.js) to dedupe on. This is reachable in practice: src/server.js's transfer handler already explicitly dedupes the two account endpoints of a transfer via `[...new Set(ends)]` (src/server.js:88-89), showing the author anticipated endpoint collisions within one call — but that same Set never includes the operator's own `url`, and the close/deposit call sites (src/server.js:70, 99) pass single-element `also` arrays with no de-dup at all. Any account owner who points their account webhook at the same URL the operator already uses (e.g. a shared internal collector, or simply copying a known endpoint) will receive every one of that account's events twice.
ROOTCAUSE: notify() in src/webhooks.js builds its delivery list as `[url, ...also].filter(Boolean)` with no de-duplication against the operator's own configured `url`, so when an account owner's webhookUrl is set to the same address as the operator's endpoint, that endpoint receives the identical signed event twice per deposit/close (and potentially per transfer) — reproduced directly: setting an owner webhook equal to the operator's URL and triggering a deposit produced two identical deliveries to the same endpoint.
================================================================================
TITLE: Literal JSON null body crashes /webhook with 500
FILE: src/server.js
LINE: 107
CATEGORY: correctness
SEVERITY: medium
VERDICT: CONFIRMED
PREEXISTING: False
FOUNDBY: ['correctness']
VERIFIEDBY: ['refute:1']
PANEL: None
SUMMARY: POST /accounts/:id/webhook evaluates `body.url` before any shape validation, so a literal JSON `null` body throws an unhandled TypeError that the catch-all turns into an opaque 500 instead of the 400 every other malformed-input case gets.
SITES: [{"file": "src/server.js", "line": 107, "title": "Literal JSON null body crashes /webhook with 500"}]
FAILURE: Any signed-in user (requireUser — not even ownership-checked yet, since `body.url` is evaluated as an argument before setWebhook's getOwnAccount runs) POSTs /accounts/<id>/webhook with raw body `null` (valid JSON, parses fine via readJson). `body.url` throws 'Cannot read properties of null (reading url)'; the dispatcher's catch-all classifies it as status 500 ('internal error') and logs a stack trace via console.error, where the project's own contract (README: 'unexpected failure is a 500 that says nothing about itself'; the existing 400 path for `{}`/array bodies) implies this foreseeable, validatable input should be a 400. Verified live against the running server: a null body on /webhook returned status 500 with {"error":"internal error"}. The same unguarded-property/destructuring pattern already exists pre-diff on POST /transfers (destructures body directly), POST /deposits, and POST /accounts/:id/interest-rate (body.interestRateBps) — confirmed those also 500 on a null body — but those are gated by requireRole('admin'); the new /webhook route reproduces the same class of bug on a broader, ordinary-member-reachable route.
ROOTCAUSE: The POST /accounts/:id/webhook handler in src/server.js reads `body.url` before any shape validation, so a literal JSON `null` request body (which readJson() parses successfully, since only a fully-empty body short-circuits to `{}`) throws an unhandled TypeError on `body.url`, which the top-level catch-all turns into an opaque 500 instead of the 400 every other malformed-input case gets — reproduced directly via an HTTP call with a JSON `null` body.

findings.short_summary: Owner-set webhook URL is unrestricted: full SSRF
findings.summary: setWebhook only checks that the owner-supplied URL parses and has an http/https scheme, so the server later fetches that exact attacker-chosen URL on every deposit, transfer, and close touching the account, letting any plain member proxy requests at arbitrary internal or third-party hosts.
findings.failure_scenario: An authenticated non-admin member opens an account, POSTs /accounts/:id/webhook with { url: 'http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/' } (accepted, 200), then closes that same account (owner-only). Reproduced live: the server issues an HMAC-signed POST — signed with the operator's own webhook secret — to that address, with no admin action anywhere in the chain. 127.0.0.1, ::1, 10.0.0.5, localhost, decimal 2130706433, hex 0x7f.0.0.1 and user:pass@host all pass the validation unchanged; deliver() uses global fetch, which follows redirects, so even a host allow-list would need separate redirect handling. docs/security.md:12-14 states as a kept invariant that the service 'never requests a URL that a user supplied, in whole or in part'; this diff does not touch that file.

findings.short_summary: Owner webhook equal to operator's double-delivers events
findings.summary: notify() builds its delivery list as `[url, ...also].filter(Boolean)` with no de-duplication against the operator's own configured url, so an account webhook pointed at the operator's endpoint gets the same event POSTed there twice (two sites: src/webhooks.js:37 and :38 are one defect).
findings.failure_scenario: With `url: 'https://hooks.example/ledger'`, calling notify('deposit.created', data, ['https://hooks.example/ledger']) sends two separate POSTs to the identical target, each independently timestamped and HMAC-signed, so the receiver cannot tell they are the same deposit — the payload {event, data, at} carries no event id to dedupe on. Reachable in practice: the transfer handler already dedupes the two account endpoints via [...new Set(ends)] (src/server.js:88-89), but that Set never includes the operator url, and the close/deposit call sites (src/server.js:70, 99) do no de-dup at all.

findings.short_summary: JSON null body on /webhook returns opaque 500
findings.summary: POST /accounts/:id/webhook evaluates `body.url` before any shape validation, so a literal JSON null body throws an unhandled TypeError that the catch-all turns into an opaque 500 instead of the 400 every other malformed-input case gets.
findings.failure_scenario: Any signed-in user (not even ownership-checked yet, since body.url is evaluated as an argument before setWebhook's getOwnAccount runs) POSTs /accounts/<id>/webhook with raw body `null` — valid JSON, parsed fine by readJson. body.url throws 'Cannot read properties of null (reading url)'; verified live, the response is 500 {"error":"internal error"} with a stack trace logged. The same pattern exists pre-diff on /transfers, /deposits and /interest-rate, but those are gated by requireRole('admin'); this new route exposes the class on an ordinary-member-reachable path.
